title: Stalk kernel span of exterior tensor quotient relations
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], S=(K→B→C) a short exact sequence of module sheaves, A a module sheaf, and r,s natural numbers with s≠0. Use exterior sheaves [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power] and module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let q:(exteriorSheaf A r) tensor (exteriorSheaf B s)→(exteriorSheaf A r) tensor (exteriorSheaf C s) send every tensor of wedges of sections to the tensor with the second wedge mapped by g. For each open V let Q(V) be the O_X(V)-span of wedge(a) tensor wedge(c) with c_j=f(d) for some j and d in K(V). For x in X let Q_x be the O_{X,x}-span of all germs at x of elements of Q(V), where V ranges over neighborhoods of x. Then the kernel of the O_{X,x}-linear stalk map q_x is contained in Q_x.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: quotient lift independence; stalk algebra portion of lem-sc-exterior-tensor-kernel-locally-spanned

proof.text: Exactness on stalks identifies C_x with B_x/im(f_x). Apply the alternating multilinear presentation of exterior powers. Wedges with an entry in im(f_x) vanish in the quotient. Conversely, modding out by their span makes a wedge independent of all quotient representatives, by expansion of one changed entry at a time, so this quotient has the universal property of the exterior power of C_x. Thus these wedges generate its kernel.

Tensor with the r-th exterior power of A_x. Right exactness of tensor products and spanning by pure wedges give the analogous tensor kernel generators. Stalks commute with the finite-sum, finite-tuple exterior and tensor presentations. On generators, the assumed formula for q gives precisely this tensor quotient map. Hence its stalk kernel is spanned by these relation tensors.

Each relation tensor contains finitely many stalk entries and a preimage under f_x for its distinguished entry. Choose representatives on a common neighborhood of x. Equality of germs allows a further shrink so that c_j=f(d) holds for sections. Their tensor is then a section of Q(V), and its germ is the relation tensor. These germs therefore generate the stalk kernel inside Q_x. The empty wedge handles r=0, and a zero stalk ring has only zero modules.

theorem exteriorTensor_stalk_kernel_le_relationSpan {X : Scheme.{v}}
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact) (A : X.Modules) (r s : ℕ) (hs : s ≠ 0)
    (q : exteriorSheaf A r ⊗ exteriorSheaf S.X₂ s ⟶
      exteriorSheaf A r ⊗ exteriorSheaf S.X₃ s)
    (hq : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (a : Fin r → A.val.obj (op U))
      (c : Fin s → S.X₂.val.obj (op U)),
      q.val.app (op U)
        (tmulSection (exteriorSheafSection A r U a)
          (exteriorSheafSection S.X₂ s U c)) =
        tmulSection (M := exteriorSheaf A r) (N := exteriorSheaf S.X₃ s)
          (exteriorSheafSection A r U a)
          (exteriorSheafSection S.X₃ s U (fun i ↦ S.g.val.app (op U) (c i))))
    (x : X) :
    LinearMap.ker (q.stalkLinearMap x) ≤ exteriorTensorRelationStalkSpan S A r s x
